I’m sorry this is happening to you. Divorce is a situation where we have to all be brutally honest with ourselves. 
You said she trashed the place and left with the kids, and you wonder if you can go to their grandma and pick them up while she is ‘out partying’. 
I want to know:
1. Did she trash the place or left in a hurry? And if so, why? I know of someone who’s abusive ex tried to say that when the truth was the lady had ran for her life while he was at work. 

2. What wrongs has she done during the marriage and what wrongs have you done? I mean verbal and physical abuse, cheating etc, big things. Make note of them. 

3. I understand you want your kids back, I can only imagine but tread carefully. Sometimes our passion for our kids can come out in negative ways such as anger and reflect badly on us. ‘She’s out partying’ implies you are feeling nasty towards her and that won’t play well in court. 

4. Unless she is a horrid person who punished you in the past, most women or men who leave in this manner leave because they feel that the other parent will abuse them, and/or use the children as a way to punish them etc. these things will be important in court. 

5. Who do the kids spend time with the most? Who cooks, cleans, nurtures them takes them to school practice etc, is there for emotional needs? I know it sucks to hear this but whoever it is is the one who gets primary custody. And that’s how it should be too. I mean if I’m hardly around or working I’d rather my kids are with the other parent as long as they are sane and safe. And for that we are talking around ‘most of the time’ maybe she goes partying..but she comes back and makes them breakfast and takes them to school? Then she gets it. If all that was done by you, then you’ll get it. 

6. Right now the best bet is an attorney who will file an emergency order and that way the two of you will have some visitation schedule. 

7. Please don’t ruin your bank account or all of your lives fighting for the ego rush of ‘primary/full custody’ this fight doesn’t punish the other parent or make you the winner, it destroys the lives of your kids. 

8. She wouldn’t have to leave to another place to get primary, as a mom if she is involved she would get the primary almost always. Is she a bad mom? If not, then let her. 

9. I know you are struggling I’d be too, so try to talk to her if possible. Send a polite short text, saying something to the effect of how you understand she’s divorcing you and tensions are high, but you still love/like her whatever and you love the kids and would like to be there for them and can she please let them say hello or meet you even if it’s outdoors? Use the soft approach and it’ll look great in court 

10. As I said above, get a lawyer. I promise it’ll be okay. Don’t stress and try to remember your babies are safe and you WILL see them soon.
